Implement an ordinary in-memory LRU cache in Python 3.12 using only the standard library.
This is a library, not a web service. No concurrency or rate-limiting is required.

Required public API in src/lru_cache.py:
  class LRUCache:
    __init__(self, capacity: int)
    get(self, key, default=None)
    put(self, key, value) -> None
    __len__(self) -> int
    keys(self) -> list  # least-recently-used to most-recently-used

capacity must be a positive built-in int: reject bool and non-int values with TypeError,
and zero/negative integers with ValueError. Keys are any hashable objects.
get hits and put operations update recency; get misses return the supplied default and
must not change recency. Updating an existing key must not evict another key or grow size.
Insertion at capacity evicts exactly the least recently used key. Preserve None/False/0
and other values exactly. Cache instances are independent. get and put must be O(1).
Do not catch TypeError for unhashable keys; ordinary dictionary semantics are sufficient.

Return full implementation files under src/ and at least one pytest file under tests/.
All files must be .py; no package installation, generated configuration, network, shell,
conftest.py, pytest hooks, test skipping, or modification of the test runner is allowed.
Tests must import `from lru_cache import LRUCache` (src/ is added to sys.path by the runner).
Include useful edge-case assertions, not placeholder tests. Independent fixed acceptance
tests will run in a separate isolated container against the same implementation.
